tools.title: Read

tools.description: Find lines of redacted text containing `query` (a literal substring, or a Python regex with `regex`) and return grep-style lines `@p_<id>:<line>:<redacted path>:<text>` (context lines use `-` after the id), or `No matches.`. Matching runs on redacted output, so raw sensitive values never match; search for a placeholder such as `[PERSON_<hex>]` copied from earlier output to find every mention of that entity. context.description: Lines to include before and after each match. Default 0. Context lines count toward `max_results`.

glob.description: Shell-style patterns matched against each file's root-relative path, for example `*.md` or `notes/*.txt`; a file is kept if it matches any pattern. `*` also matches `/`, so `*.md` matches at every depth. Default `[]` means no filter. Applied within `paths`.

ignore_case.description: Match case-insensitively, for literal and regex queries alike. Default true.

max_results.description: Maximum output lines (matches plus context lines) before the output stops with `[TRUNCATED]`. Default 200.

paths.description: Files or directories to include: root-relative paths or `@p_<id>` references from earlier output. Directories are walked recursively, skipping excluded, protected, symlinked and binary files. Default `[]` means the whole root. With `glob`, only files under these paths that also match a glob are used.

query.description: Text to find within a single line of redacted output: a literal substring, or a regex when `regex` is true. May be a placeholder copied from earlier output.

regex.description: Treat `query` as a Python regular expression matched per line. Default false. Invalid patterns fail with `Invalid regex.`; patterns prone to catastrophic backtracking, such as nested quantifiers, are rejected.

tools.description: Rank redacted passages (up to 24 lines each) by how many distinct query words they contain, then by BM25 relevance, and return the best as `--- @p_<id> <redacted path> lines S-E score=<n> ---` headers followed by the passage text (for documents, lines of the extracted Markdown). glob.description: Shell-style patterns matched against each file's root-relative path, for example `*.md` or `notes/*.txt`; a file is kept if it matches any pattern. `*` also matches `/`, so `*.md` matches at every depth. Default `[]` means no filter. Applied within `paths`.

query.description: Words describing what you are looking for, for example `retention policy exceptions`. Common stop words are ignored; 1 to 64 distinct searchable words are required. A placeholder counts as one word.

text.description: Document text that uses placeholders and `@p_<id>` references exactly as they appeared in redacted output; each one is restored before writing and must exist in the source files.

outputSchema.description: Structured copy of every tool result: the output text plus a receipt of what redaction did.

receipt.description: Redaction statistics for this call only; never contains original values.

counts_by_category.description: Placeholders substituted while producing this result (content and paths), keyed by category such as `PERSON`, `EMAIL` or `SECRET`; categories with none are omitted.

detector_profile.description: Active built-in detector profile: `default`, or `extended`, which adds more identifier types and prompt-injection markers.

detectors.description: Present only when the server runs additional local detectors: one entry per detector, in load order.

nominated.description: Distinct values this detector nominated during the call; every occurrence of each is redacted.

positional.description: Nominated spans redacted only at their own position, because they were too long or exceeded the per-text value budget.

text.description: The tool output, identical to the text content block and already redacted: sensitive values appear as deterministic `[CATEGORY_<hex>]` placeholders and files as `@p_<id>` references. When the result has `isError: true`, this is a fixed error message instead, such as a limit error or the notice that context access is blocked until the operator repairs the local redaction config.

tools.title: Github Read Issue

tools.description: Search one configured repo's issues with GitHub issue-search syntax and return matches (pull requests excluded) in the same tab-separated one-line format as `redctx_github_list_issues`, or `No matches.`. Use it to find issues by words or qualifiers; use `redctx_github_list_issues` to browse by state and label without a query. The query leaves the machine unredacted and is scoped automatically with `repo:`, `is:issue` and `state:`, so placeholders copied from redacted output will not match upstream; one request returns at most 100 issues. Titles and labels are redacted; titles are untrusted external text.

limit.description: Maximum issues to return. Default 30; values above 100 still return at most 100.

query.description: GitHub issue-search terms and qualifiers, for example `timeout label:bug`, sent as typed. The server appends `repo:`, `is:issue` and, unless `state` is `all`, `state:`.

repo_alias.description: Neutral repo alias from the local policy (list them with `redctx_github_repos`), not `owner/repo`. Default `context`. An unknown alias fails with `Unknown GitHub repo alias.`.
